 Justin Edwards' 76ers future is becoming clearer with every game he misses 
 Nick Nurse clearly doesn't trust Justin Edwards. By Nathan Doyle | Nov 18, 2026, 9:06 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Camden, NJ, USA; Philadelphia 76ers Justin Edwards poses for a photo during media day on September 28, 2026. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Actions speak louder than words, and every game Nick Nurse refuses to play Justin Edwards, the 22-year-old's future feels more inevitable. Edwards has been a constant in the ever-changing Philadelphia 76ers' landscape over the last three seasons, but his journey with the franchise appears to be coming to a very uneventful end.
--> Actions speak louder than words, and every game Nick Nurse refuses to play Justin Edwards, the 22-year-old's future feels more inevitable. Edwards has been a constant in the ever-changing Philadelphia 76ers' landscape over the last three seasons, but his journey with the franchise appears to be coming to a very uneventful end.
 During his rookie year in Philadelphia, Edwards was something of a phenomenon. After going undrafted in the 2024 draft, the Kentucky alum burst onto the scene with the 76ers. His spot-up shooting, selfless attitude, and defensive hustle were a shining light in a dark period for the franchise. 
--> During his rookie year in Philadelphia, Edwards was something of a phenomenon. After going undrafted in the 2024 draft, the Kentucky alum burst onto the scene with the 76ers. His spot-up shooting, selfless attitude, and defensive hustle were a shining light in a dark period for the franchise. 
 Many believed Edwards would hold an important rotational role for years to come as he recorded 10.1 points and 3.4 rebounds, shooting 45.5 percent from the floor and 36.3 percent from deep. Edwards was never expected to become the face of the franchise, but few could have anticipated how quickly his stock would fall.

 Edwards' fate with the 76ers feels somewhat inevitable

 It was apparent during Edwards' second year with the 76ers that Nick Nurse wasn't as excited about his potential. The reasons behind his diminished role were unclear. Maybe the Sixers' head coach was trying to teach a young player a valuable lesson in resilience? Considering this 'lesson' has continued into the 2026-27 season, it's fair to suggest Nurse doesn't believe Edwards can make a positive contribution to the team.

Maybe the Sixers' head coach was trying to teach a young player a valuable lesson in resilience? Considering this 'lesson' has continued into the 2026-27 season, it's fair to suggest Nurse doesn't believe Edwards can make a positive contribution to the team.
 Edwards has featured in just 6 of the 76ers' 15 fixtures this season, averaging 2.5 minutes, 0.8 points, and 0.7 rebounds per game. His numbers are a victim of circumstance; no player can make an impact in such a small amount of time.

 To make matters worse, Edwards was snubbed for a recall from the Sixers' G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats, in recent days, while the franchise did recall Labaron Philon Jr. After another game in Delaware, Edwards returned to Philadelphia, but his inconsistent performances at that level will undoubtedly have contributed to the decision.

 The forward has averaged 12.5 points, 2 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game, while registering a -10 point differential. This two-game sample size was a chance for Edwards to make a statement his head coach couldn't ignore. It was a chance to fight through adversity and force a place in the Sixers' rotation. Unfortunately, his showings didn't make the grade.

Unfortunately, his showings didn't make the grade. 
 Edwards' underdog journey has been wonderful to watch during his time in Philadelphia, but his recent usage suggests his story with the franchise is coming to an end. Nurse has established a clear eight-man rotation that doesn't include Edwards, and it's hard to see a circumstance in which that would change.
